title: Unpaid Host Shares Set Against a Claim Payment
content:
What a host owes on their Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment is set against the money released to them, and how much of it turns on whether cover on the enrolment still stands in force.

- Where a share raised on the enrolment in the twelve months before stands unpaid and cover on it stands in force, the whole of what stands unpaid is set against the payment.
- Where a share raised in that period stands unpaid and cover on it does not stand in force, half of it is set against the payment.
- Where no share raised in that period stands unpaid, nothing is set against it.

What is set against the payment is deducted last.

### Worked illustration (hypothetical figures)

Suppose 800 stands unpaid on the enrolment and a share was raised on it within the twelve months before.

| Cover on the enrolment | Set against the payment |
|---|---|
| in force | 800.00 |
| paused, fallen away or ended | 400.00 |

Where nothing stands unpaid, or where no share was raised on the enrolment within the twelve months before, nothing at all is set against the payment.

### Where the facts come from

The shares counted are those raised on this enrolment within the twelve months before, what stands unpaid is the amount owed by the host on the enrolment, and cover stands in force where the enrolment is active.
